meta.description: A/B TWIN of krea2_character_lora, identical in every value except timestep_type: shift instead of linear. It exists to settle a contested setting by measurement instead of argument (CLAUDE.md's rule for exactly this). The disagreement, one source each: LoRA Dataset Studio / RunComfy call linear the Krea-canonical choice, which is why every other Krea 2 preset here ships it; musubi-tuner's own docs/krea2.md - kohya, on the trainer that produced every Krea 2 run this fork trusts - recommends shift sampling instead, --timestep_sampling shift with --discrete_flow_shift 2.5, saying it matches the K2 inference time-shift at 1024x1024, or --timestep_sampling krea2_shift for a resolution-aware schedule per sample. This trainer's shift IS that resolution-aware schedule, not a fixed 2.5: toolkit/samplers/custom_flowmatch_sampler.py's shift branch is commented 'matches inference dynamic shifting' and reads the Krea-specific exponential mu endpoints krea2.py sets (base_shift 0.5 at 256-res to max_shift 1.15 at 1280-res, use_dynamic_shifting true, time_shift_type exponential), per sample from the actual latent size. Upstream's 2026-09-16 patch_size fix is what made its token count correct - runs before that commit computed the wrong one, so any older shift result is void. HOW TO USE IT: run this and krea2_character_lora on the SAME dataset, same seed, same step count, then compare sample grids at matched steps - likeness, prompt adherence, and whether detail holds at non-1024 aspect buckets, which is where a resolution-aware schedule should show up first if it shows up at all. Nothing else differs, so the difference is attributable. Record the result in docs/krea2_field_template_2026_09.md section 7 and, if shift wins, the other Krea 2 presets follow. UNRESOLVED and UNMEASURED as shipped: this preset is the experiment, not the recommendation - the field template that motivated it never recorded which sampling its good runs used.
